selection_principle: Predefined multi-criterion selection based on discrimination, calibration, stability, interpretability, parsimony, and implementation feasibility; not AUROC alone.
selection_rationale: M1 improved AUROC, AUPRC, and Brier score over M0 for all four algorithms with paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals excluding the null.
XGBoost achieved the highest AUROC and AUPRC, but its paired discrimination gains over RF were small and the 95% confidence intervals included zero.

RF achieved the lowest Brier score among M1 models while maintaining strong discrimination, clinically relevant sensitivity, high specificity, and straightforward SHAP-based interpretation and deployment.
RF was therefore selected as the best overall trade-off under the prespecified multi-criterion rule, not as a claim of universal statistical superiority over all alternatives.

final_refit.note: This full-data inner-CV value is a tuning/refit diagnostic and must not be reported as the generalization performance estimate. Primary performance estimates are from outer cross-validation.

explainability.method: SHAP TreeExplainer on the full-data refitted M1-RF model
explainability.interpretation_constraint: SHAP values describe predictive attribution and must not be interpreted causally.

calibration_caution: The selected RF had calibration intercept -0.6335 and slope 0.8728. Raw predicted probabilities should therefore not be presented as externally validated absolute clinical risk. External validation and, if appropriate, recalibration are required before clinical use.
